blocks.text: This name is found in Suratul Ikhlaas.
'As Samad' means (as-Sayyid al-'Adheem) The Great Master who has complete and perfect knowledge, wisdom, forbearance, power, honour, greatness and is Perfect in all His Attributes and descriptions.

So He possesses great and encompassing descriptions. All of the creation depend upon Him. All beings, even the most hidden, call upon Him in all their affairs. They do not have a Lord other than Him. They do not have anyone other than Him that they can call on to rectify their religious or worldly matters. They take refuge in Him at times of calamities and troubles. They humbly implore Him when disasters and hard times strike. They ask Him for help during hardships and trials. This is because they know that He can meet their needs and remove the calamities due to His Perfect and complete Knowledge, encompassing Mercy and Compassion, His Perfection, great Ability, His Honour and His Authority.
Ibn Jareer at Tabaree narrated in his Tafseer from 'Abdullaah bin 'Abbaas that he said,

As Samad The Self-Sufficient Master: The Master who is complete in his Mastership; The Sublime who is complete in His Sublimity; The Great who is complete in His Greatness; The Forbearing who is complete in His Forbearance and Clemency; The Rich who is complete in His Richness; The Wise who is complete in His Wisdom. He is the One who is complete and perfect in types of Exaltedness and Mastership. He is Allaah, the One removed from every defect who deserves these descriptions which are only befitting to Him.
blocks.ref: Tafseer at-Tabaree (24/736 At Turki Print); Suyooti in 'Dur al Manthoor' (15/780)

keyPoints: As-Samad is found in Suratul Ikhlaas.
As-Samad means the Great Master who has complete and perfect knowledge, wisdom, forbearance, power, honour and greatness, and is Perfect in all His Attributes.
All of the creation depend upon Him and call upon Him in all their affairs, taking refuge in Him in calamities and hardships.
They turn to Him because He can meet their needs and remove calamities due to His perfect Knowledge, Mercy, Ability, Honour and Authority.
Ibn 'Abbaas explained As-Samad as the One complete in Mastership, Sublimity, Greatness, Forbearance, Richness and Wisdom.

evidence.text: Say (O Muhammad): "He is Allah, (the) One. Allah-us-Samad (The Self-Sufficient Master, Whom all creatures need). He begets not, nor was He begotten; and there is none co-equal or comparable unto Him."
Ibn 'Abbaas: "As Samad: The Master who is complete in his Mastership ... He is the One who is complete and perfect in types of Exaltedness and Mastership."

recall.a: The Self-Sufficient Master: the Great Master who has complete and perfect knowledge, wisdom, forbearance, power, honour, greatness and is Perfect in all His Attributes and descriptions.

recall.q: In which Soorah is the Name As-Samad found?

recall.a: The Master complete in His Mastership, the Sublime complete in His Sublimity, the Great complete in His Greatness, the Forbearing complete in His Forbearance, the Rich complete in His Richness, the Wise complete in His Wisdom.

recall.q: Why do all beings call upon As-Samad in their needs?
recall.a: Because they know He can meet their needs and remove the calamities due to His perfect Knowledge, encompassing Mercy and Compassion, His Perfection, great Ability, Honour and Authority.
